Identifying mistakes mirrors computing the discrepancy between actual and target outputs; the causal relation (error detection) aligns.
Students' individual work maps to intermediate computational units that mediate between input and output; the structural correspondence is clear.

structural_issues: Teacher feedback is typically discrete and qualitative, whereas gradients are continuous numerical values, which may weaken the precision of the analogy.
The analogy assumes a linear chain of responsibility, while neural networks can have branching and skip connections that are not captured by a simple teacher‑student chain.
Students modify their future contributions, but weight updates affect the model instantly; the temporal mismatch is a minor inconsistency.
result.rationale: All six source‑target correspondences preserve the essential roles and causal mechanisms of backpropagation; only minor domain differences (qualitative vs quantitative feedback, linear vs network topology) introduce slight stretches, but they do not break logical consistency.
